questions.q: You can't ride your bicycle without falling. What should you do?
o: Keep practising a little every day
Give the bicycle to someone else because you will never learn
Only ride when nobody is watching you
questions.why: Practising a little each day helps you learn.

questions.q: Your kite won't fly. What can you try?
o: Run against the wind and try again
Throw the kite away and go home sad
Wait for someone to fly it for you all day
questions.why: Trying a new way often solves the problem.

questions.q: You got many sums wrong. What can you say?
o: "I will find my mistakes and try again."
"Maths is too hard, I'm not good at it at all."
questions.why: Finding mistakes helps you learn.

questions.q: Your drawing went wrong. What can you do?
o: Turn the mistake into something new in the picture
Tear it up and say you can't draw anything nice ever
questions.why: Mistakes can become new ideas.

questions.q: It rained on sports day and the race was cancelled. What can you do?
o: Play an indoor game with friends
Stay sad the whole day and don't talk to anyone at home
questions.why: When plans change, finding another fun thing helps.

questions.q: You lost your favourite eraser. What is a good next step?
o: Look for it calmly, then use another one
Cry until someone buys a new one for you right now
questions.why: Staying calm helps you solve the problem.

questions.q: You can't reach the top shelf. What can you do?
o: Climb on a wobbly chair by yourself to get it quickly
questions.why: Asking for help is smart and safe.

questions.q: You forgot your lines in the school play. What can you do?
o: Smile, take a breath, and say what you remember
Run off the stage and hide behind the curtain for the rest
questions.why: Carrying on bravely is what actors do.

questions.q: You missed the bus. What should you do?
o: Tell a grown-up so they can help
Walk alone to school on the busy road
questions.why: Telling a grown-up keeps you safe.

questions.q: Your block tower keeps falling. What can you try?
o: Build it taller and faster so it falls later
questions.why: Changing the way you build can fix the problem.

questions.q: You came last in the race. What can you tell yourself?
o: "I finished the race. I'll get faster."
"Everyone saw me lose, so I'm never racing again."
questions.why: Finishing is something to be proud of.

questions.q: Your plant didn't grow. What can you do?
o: Find out if it needs more water or sun
Throw the pot away because plants don't like you
questions.why: Finding the reason helps you try again.

questions.q: You can't open your tiffin box. What can you do?
o: Ask a friend or teacher for help
Bang it hard on the floor until it opens
questions.why: Asking for help solves the problem quickly.

questions.q: Your sandcastle broke. What can you do?
o: Build a new one, even better
Sit and be sad until it is time to go home
questions.why: You can always start again.

questions.q: You can't find your shoes and it's time to go. What helps?
o: Look in the places you were today
Go without shoes even though the road is hot
Cry and say you can't go
questions.why: Thinking about where you were helps you find things.

questions.q: You spelled a word wrong in a test. What will help next time?
o: Practise the word a few times
Never write that word again in your whole life
questions.why: Practice helps you remember.

questions.q: Your friend is busy and can't play with you. What can you do?
o: Find another fun thing to do
Sit at the door and wait for your friend all day long
Say they are not your friend
questions.why: You can find other fun when plans change.

questions.q: You dropped your ice cream. What can you think?
o: "Oops! Maybe next time I'll hold it with two hands."
"This is the worst day ever and everything is ruined."
questions.why: Small problems are okay, and we can learn from them.

questions.q: You find a puzzle too hard. What can you do?
o: Put it away and say puzzles are only for big children
questions.why: Starting with an easy part helps with hard puzzles.

questions.q: You were afraid to jump in the pool. What is a brave step?
o: Sit on the edge with your feet in, with a grown-up next to you
Say you are not scared and walk away from the pool for ever
questions.why: Small steps help you become brave.

questions.q: Your painting got wet in the rain. What can you do?
o: Let it dry and fix the spots
Throw it away and say you'll never paint again
questions.why: Many things can be fixed with a little care.

questions.q: You can't tie your shoelaces yet. What helps?
o: Practise slowly with someone showing you
Wear shoes with laces open and trip over them
questions.why: Practising with help teaches new skills.

questions.q: Your team lost a game. What can you say to your team?
o: "We lost because some of you were too slow today."
questions.why: Kind team talk helps everyone try again.

questions.q: You felt shy and didn't answer in class. What can you do tomorrow?
o: Try to answer one easy question
Hide behind your bag so the teacher can't see you
Ask your friend to answer for you every time
questions.why: One small step makes you braver.

questions.q: Your toy car broke. What can you do?
o: Ask Papa if it can be fixed
Break it more because it doesn't work anyway
Cry for a new one all day
questions.why: Some things can be fixed if we ask for help.

questions.q: You lost a game of snakes and ladders. What can you do?
o: Throw the dice away so no one can play
Say you never liked the game
questions.why: Playing again is a fun way to bounce back.

questions.q: You forgot your homework at home. What should you do?
o: Tell your teacher honestly and bring it tomorrow
Say your dog tore it up, so the teacher won't be cross with you
questions.why: Being honest and fixing it is the right way.

questions.q: You can't whistle yet. What can you do?
o: Keep trying a little each day
Decide you are just a person who can never whistle
questions.why: Trying a little each day helps you learn.

questions.q: You fell and scraped your knee while playing. What can you do?
o: Clean it, put a plaster on, and rest
Keep running fast even though it really hurts a lot
questions.why: Taking care of a hurt helps you get back to play.

questions.q: The shop is out of your favourite biscuits. What can you do?
o: Cry and refuse to eat anything else for the rest of the week
questions.why: Trying something new can be fun.

questions.q: You read a word wrong out loud. What can you do?
o: Read it again correctly and carry on
Stop reading and close the book so nobody hears you
questions.why: Fixing a small mistake and moving on is brave.

questions.q: Your crayons broke. What can you do?
o: Stop colouring because broken crayons can never work
questions.why: Broken crayons still colour!

questions.q: You don't understand the teacher's words. What can you do?
o: Ask, "Can you please say it again?"
Pretend you understood and hope it doesn't matter
questions.why: Asking questions helps you learn.

questions.q: Your balloon popped. What can you think?
o: "Nothing nice ever lasts for me, not even balloons."
questions.why: Remembering the fun helps you feel better.

questions.q: It's too hot to play outside. What can you do?
o: Play a game in the shade or indoors
Play in the hot sun anyway without water
questions.why: Changing plans helps when the weather is bad.

questions.q: You forgot your water bottle. What can you do?
o: Ask the teacher where to get water
Stay thirsty all day so nobody knows you forgot
Drink from someone's bottle without asking
questions.why: Asking for help solves the problem.

questions.q: You can't do a cartwheel. What can you do?
o: Practise on soft grass with a grown-up
Try it on the hard floor by yourself many times
questions.why: Safe practice helps you learn.

questions.q: Your puzzle is missing a piece. What can you do?
o: Look around carefully, or make a piece from paper
Throw the whole puzzle away because it's ruined now
questions.why: There's often a way to fix a problem.

questions.q: Your friend can't come to your birthday. What can you do?
o: Plan to celebrate with them another day
Cancel your whole birthday party because of it
questions.why: Planning another day keeps the fun going.

questions.q: You couldn't finish your painting in class. What can you do?
o: Ask if you can finish it later
Throw it in the bin because it is not finished
Say it's finished when it's not
questions.why: Asking for more time helps you finish your work.

questions.q: Your sister knocked down your Lego. What can you do?
o: Tell her how you feel and build it again
Knock down all her toys so she knows how it feels
questions.why: Talking and rebuilding helps you move on.

questions.q: Your song at the concert went wrong. What can you say to yourself?
o: "I'm the worst singer and everyone laughed at me."
questions.why: Practising more helps you get better.

questions.q: You lose a button on your shirt at school. What can you do?
o: Tell the teacher and wear your sweater
Hide in the corner the whole day so nobody sees
questions.why: Telling a grown-up helps you fix small problems.

questions.q: You can't count to 100 yet. What can you do?
o: Practise counting a bit more each day
Say you'll never need big numbers anyway
questions.why: Little practice each day helps.

questions.q: You got lost in a big shop. What should you do?
o: Stay where you are and ask a shop helper
Walk out of the shop to look for your family
questions.why: Staying put and asking a helper keeps you safe.

questions.q: Your new shoes hurt your feet. What can you do?
o: Tell your parents so they can help
Keep wearing them and say nothing even though it hurts
questions.why: Telling someone helps solve problems.

questions.q: Your friend says your idea is bad. What can you do?
o: Ask what they think could make it better
Never share any of your ideas with anyone again, so nobody says that
Say their ideas are bad too
questions.why: Asking how to improve makes ideas stronger.

questions.q: You can't swim yet but your friends can. What can you do?
o: Jump in with them anyway in the deep end
Stay away from the pool forever
questions.why: Learning step by step is the safe way.

questions.q: You missed a goal in football. What can you say?
o: "I'm useless at football, I should just watch."
questions.why: Trying again is how you get better.

questions.q: Your birthday cake fell. What can you do?
o: Laugh and eat it from the plate
Cry and say your birthday is ruined forever now
questions.why: A fallen cake still tastes good!

questions.q: You were scared of a dog barking. What helps?
o: Stand still, stay calm, and call a grown-up
Run fast and scream so it barks louder
questions.why: Staying calm and getting help keeps you safe.

questions.q: Your answer was wrong in front of the class. What can you do?
o: Listen to the right answer and learn it
Decide never to answer again in front of anyone
questions.why: Learning from wrong answers helps you grow.

questions.q: You couldn't finish a book. What can you do?
o: Read a few pages each day
Say books are boring and stop reading for good
questions.why: A few pages each day finishes any book.

questions.q: Your swing broke. What can you do?
o: Tell a grown-up and play on something else
Keep sitting on the broken swing and try to fix it alone
questions.why: Telling a grown-up keeps everyone safe.

questions.q: You lost a game of tag. What can you say?
o: "You're all too fast, I'm going home now."
questions.why: Enjoying the game matters more than winning.

questions.q: You can't sleep because of noise. What can you do?
o: Tell your parents and try a calm story
Get up and play loud music too
questions.why: Asking for help solves the problem.

questions.q: You made a mess of your room. What can you do?
o: Clean one corner at a time
Close the door and leave it forever
questions.why: Small steps make big jobs easy.

questions.q: You can't jump rope yet. What can you do?
o: Practise slowly, a few jumps at a time
Jump very fast to finish quickly and fall
questions.why: Practising slowly helps you learn.

questions.q: Your friend is moving to another city. What can you do?
o: Make a plan to send letters or call
Say goodbye angrily and not talk to them before they go
questions.why: Staying in touch keeps friendships alive.

questions.q: Your crayon drawing smudged. What can you do?
o: Turn the smudge into clouds or smoke
Tear it and say drawing is too hard for you
questions.why: Mistakes can become creative ideas.

questions.q: You fail a unit test in a subject you usually do well in. What's the best first step?
o: Look at what went wrong and make a short plan to fix it
Decide the subject has become too hard for you and drop the effort
questions.why: Analysing the problem turns a setback into a plan.

questions.q: Your science project didn't work on the first try. What should you do?
o: Change one thing at a time and test again
Change everything at once and hope something works
Give up and choose an easier project
Copy a project from the internet
questions.why: Testing one change at a time shows what works.

questions.q: You didn't get selected for the school band. What's a good next step?
o: Ask the teacher what to practise and try again next term
Decide music is not for you and give your instrument to someone else
questions.why: Feedback and practice lead to better chances.

questions.q: Your group project partner falls sick before the deadline. What do you do?
o: Divide their work among the group and inform the teacher
Do nothing and let the project fail
Complain to everyone about your partner
Ask the teacher to cancel the whole project because one member is sick
questions.why: Adapting quickly and communicating keeps the project on track.

questions.q: You're struggling to learn a new language. What helps most?
o: Practise a little daily and use it in real conversations
Study for many hours once a week only, so you finish more chapters together
Decide you have no talent for languages
questions.why: Daily practice and real use build language skills.

questions.q: You broke your arm before the sports meet. What's a good way to cope?
o: Help the team in other ways and plan your recovery
Feel useless and stay away from the team
Stay home and refuse to watch the meet because it makes you sad
questions.why: Finding new ways to contribute helps you stay positive.

questions.q: Your exam is tomorrow and you feel unprepared. What's best?
o: Revise the most important topics and sleep on time
Stay up all night trying to learn every chapter in the book
questions.why: Focusing on key topics and rest gives the best result.

questions.q: You keep losing at chess to your friend. What helps?
o: Study your lost games to find your mistakes
Play only against easier opponents so you can win more often
questions.why: Learning from losses improves your game.

questions.q: Your friend group splits up and you feel alone. What's a good step?
o: Reach out to other classmates and join new activities
Stay alone and wait for your old group to come back together
questions.why: New connections help you bounce back.

questions.q: Your phone breaks and you lose all your notes. What's best?
o: Ask classmates to share notes and start backing up
Give up on those chapters and hope they don't come in the exam
questions.why: Asking for help and planning ahead fixes the problem.

questions.q: You get a bad haircut before a family function. What helps?
o: Laugh it off and remember hair grows back
Refuse to go to the function at all
Hide your head under a cap all week until it grows out
questions.why: Keeping problems in proportion helps you move on.

questions.q: You're nervous about moving to a new school. What helps?
o: Learn about the school and focus on one new friend at a time
Expect the worst and stay quiet
Act tough and keep to yourself so nobody tries to bother you
questions.why: Small steps make big changes easier.

questions.q: Your favourite team keeps losing. What can you learn?
o: Support them through good and bad times
Switch to supporting whichever team is winning this season
questions.why: Loyalty through hard times is part of resilience.

questions.q: You can't solve a maths problem after many tries. What's best?
o: Take a break, then try a different method or ask for help
Keep trying the very same method for another hour until it works
questions.why: A break and a new approach often unlock problems.

questions.q: Your stage performance had a mistake. What's a good way to see it?
o: Most people didn't notice; I'll learn from it
"It wasn't my fault, the sound system made me miss my cue."
questions.why: Seeing mistakes realistically helps you keep going.

questions.q: You lost your library book. What's the responsible step?
o: Tell the librarian and offer to pay or replace it
Avoid the library from now on
Tell the librarian someone must have stolen it from your bag
questions.why: Owning the problem and fixing it is responsible.

questions.q: Your sibling gets better marks and you feel low. What helps?
o: Focus on your own progress and strengths
Stop trying because you'll never be as good
Ask parents to stop praising them
questions.why: Comparing with your own past is fairer and more motivating.

questions.q: Your cricket team keeps losing. As captain, what do you do?
o: Review what's going wrong and practise those skills
Change the whole team before the next match and start from scratch
questions.why: Finding and fixing weak areas helps the team improve.

questions.q: You forgot to submit your assignment on time. What should you do?
o: Tell the teacher honestly and ask if you can submit late
Tell the teacher the internet stopped working at the last minute
questions.why: Honesty gives you a chance to fix the mistake.

questions.q: Your painting didn't win the competition. What's healthy?
o: Enjoy what you made and see the winners' work for ideas
Tell your friends the judges don't really understand art
questions.why: Learning from others helps you improve.

questions.q: You're finding it hard to wake up early for school. What helps?
o: Go to bed earlier and keep a routine
Set ten alarms in a row and snooze each one until you finally get up
questions.why: Routines solve morning struggles.

questions.q: Your best friend moves away. What can help?
o: Keep in touch and also make new friends
Stop making close friends so you never feel this sad again
questions.why: Staying connected and opening up helps you cope.

questions.q: You keep making the same spelling mistakes. What helps?
o: Make a list of tricky words and practise them
Use only short, easy words so you never make spelling mistakes
questions.why: Targeted practice fixes repeated mistakes.

questions.q: You're not chosen as class monitor. What can you do?
o: Help the monitor and show leadership in other ways
Complain to your parents and ask them to talk to the class teacher
questions.why: Leadership can be shown without a title.

questions.q: Your model rocket crashes on the first launch. What do you do?
o: Find out what went wrong and rebuild
Decide rockets are too hard and choose an easier project
questions.why: Investigating failure is how scientists succeed.

questions.q: You keep getting distracted while studying. What helps?
o: Keep your phone in another room and study in short blocks
Study with the TV on softly so the room doesn't feel boring
questions.why: Removing distractions and short blocks improve focus.

questions.q: You have a bad day at school. What helps you feel better?
o: Talk to someone and do something you enjoy
Keep it all inside so nobody at home has to worry about you
Take it out on your family
Decide every day will be bad
questions.why: Talking and enjoying something helps you reset.

questions.q: Your family can't afford an expensive trip your friends are taking. What helps?
o: Plan a fun day trip nearby with family
Tell your friends you are going on a trip too, so you don't feel left out
questions.why: Finding fun within your means keeps you positive.

questions.q: You forget your lines at a speech competition. What's best?
o: Pause, look at your notes, and continue
Stop speaking, say "sorry, I forgot" and walk off the stage
questions.why: Pausing and carrying on shows composure.

questions.q: You keep losing badminton matches. What should you try?
o: Practise one skill at a time, like your serve
Buy a new, more expensive racquet so your shots get better
questions.why: Focused practice improves skills.

questions.q: You failed to get into a summer camp. What's a good response?
o: Look for another camp or plan your own summer project
Stay at home all summer and wait until next year's camp
questions.why: Finding another path keeps you moving forward.

questions.q: You were teased for your new braces. What helps?
o: Remember they're temporary and talk to a trusted adult if teasing continues
Tease them back about something of theirs so they stop
questions.why: Perspective and support help you handle teasing.

questions.q: Your project file got deleted. What should you do?
o: Check backups, then redo it with a plan
questions.why: Staying calm and planning helps you recover.

questions.q: You feel you're bad at sports. What's a good mindset?
o: Some people are born good, you aren't
questions.why: A growth mindset helps you improve.

questions.q: Your favourite shop closed. What can you do?
questions.why: Adapting to changes is part of resilience.

questions.q: You missed a week of school due to illness. What's best?
o: Ask friends and teachers for notes and catch up step by step
questions.why: Step-by-step catching up works best.

questions.q: Your experiment gives a strange result. What should you do?
o: Check your steps and repeat the experiment
Change the result to look right
questions.why: Repeating and checking is good science.

questions.q: You lost your temper in a game and feel bad. What helps?
o: Apologise and plan how to calm down next time
questions.why: Learning from mistakes helps you grow.

questions.q: You can't afford a costly tuition class your friends attend. What helps?
o: Use free resources and study groups
Feel you'll fall behind for sure
questions.why: Free resources and peers can be just as helpful.

questions.q: You keep getting nervous in exams and forget answers. What helps?
o: Practise with timed mock tests at home
questions.why: Practice in exam-like conditions reduces nerves.

questions.q: Your dance group's performance got cancelled. What can you do?
o: Record the dance and share it with family
Feel all the practice was wasted
questions.why: Finding another way to share your work keeps the joy.

questions.q: You were blamed unfairly for a broken window. What helps?
o: Calmly explain the facts and ask the teacher to check
questions.why: Calm facts help find the truth.

questions.q: You missed the school trip because you were sick. What can you do?
o: Ask friends to share photos and stories
questions.why: Sharing experiences helps you feel included.

questions.q: You find it hard to make friends. What's a good start?
o: Join a club about something you like
questions.why: Shared interests make friendships easier.

questions.q: You keep forgetting your homework. What can help?
o: Write it in a planner every day
Ask friends to remind you daily
questions.why: Simple systems help you stay organised.

questions.q: Your art supplies were ruined by water. What can you do?
o: Use what's left and get creative
Stop art until you get new supplies
questions.why: Creativity can work with less.

questions.q: You got a low score in a quiz you studied for. What's useful?
o: Find out how you studied and change your method
Study more hours in the same way
questions.why: Changing methods can be more useful than more hours.

questions.q: Your favourite teacher leaves the school. What helps?
o: Give them a thank-you note and stay open to the new teacher
Refuse to like the new teacher
questions.why: Gratitude and openness help with change.

questions.q: You're scared of failing your music exam. What helps?
o: Practise the tricky parts and imagine playing calmly
Avoid practising to avoid feeling scared
questions.why: Practice and positive imagining build confidence.

questions.q: Your friends didn't like your idea for a game. What's good?
o: Ask what they'd change and improve it together
questions.why: Improving ideas together is how good ideas grow.

questions.q: You lost your way on a trekking trip. What's the safest step?
o: Stay where you are and call or signal for help
questions.why: Staying put and signalling helps rescuers find you.

questions.q: Your bicycle gets a flat tyre on the way to school. What should you do?
o: Walk it to the nearest repair shop or call home
Leave the cycle on the road
questions.why: Finding a safe solution keeps you moving.

questions.q: You were dropped from the debate team. What can help?
o: Ask for feedback and practise for the next selection
questions.why: Feedback helps you come back stronger.

questions.q: You made a mistake that cost your team a match. What's best?
o: Own it, learn from it, and keep training
questions.why: Owning mistakes builds respect and resilience.

questions.q: You missed a deadline for a competition. What can you do?
o: Note the next deadline and set reminders
questions.why: Planning prevents repeats.

questions.q: Your plant project died before submission. What's best?
o: Explain what happened and what you learned
Buy a plant and pretend it's yours
questions.why: Honest explanations and learning count in science.

questions.q: You feel tired of practising piano every day. What helps?
o: Set small goals and reward yourself
Practise for hours once a week
questions.why: Small goals make practice more rewarding.

questions.q: You keep losing your pens. What can you try?
o: Keep a fixed place for them in your bag
questions.why: Simple habits fix repeated problems.

questions.q: Your team presentation failed because the projector broke. What helps?
o: Present using the board and printouts
questions.why: Being flexible helps you handle surprises.

questions.q: You feel you're behind in maths compared to others. What's a good step?
o: Go back to the basics you missed and build up
questions.why: Strong basics help you catch up.

questions.q: You were scared to try out for the school play. What's a brave step?
o: Audition for a small role first
Ask a friend to audition for you
questions.why: Small roles build confidence.

questions.q: You lost a pet. What can help?
o: Remember the happy times and talk about your feelings
questions.why: Sharing feelings helps with grief.

questions.q: A storm cancels your birthday party. What can you do?
o: Have a small party at home with family
questions.why: Adapting plans saves the celebration.

questions.q: You don't get the stream you wanted in Class 11. What's a resilient response?
o: Explore what the new stream offers and plan your next options
Blame your teachers and parents, and keep asking to switch until they agree
questions.why: Exploring new paths keeps opportunities open.

questions.q: You get rejected from a competition you prepared months for. What's the healthiest response?
o: Allow yourself to feel it, then ask for feedback and set a new goal
Decide competitions are pointless and focus only on marks from now on
questions.why: Feeling, learning and refocusing build resilience.

questions.q: Your startup idea at a school fair gets no interest. What's best?
o: Talk to visitors to learn why and improve the idea
Drop the idea and never try again
Copy the most popular stall's idea for the next fair so you get visitors
questions.why: Feedback from users improves ideas.

questions.q: You fall sick in the middle of exam preparation. What's a smart approach?
o: Rest to recover, then adjust your study plan
Keep studying through the illness all night so you don't fall behind
questions.why: Recovering first and re-planning is wiser than pushing through.

questions.q: Your family faces a financial setback. What's a helpful mindset?
o: Focus on what you can control and support your family
Worry constantly about the future so you're ready for the worst
questions.why: Focusing on what you can control reduces helplessness.

questions.q: You receive a lower score than expected in a mock JEE/NEET test. What's the best next step?
o: Analyse every wrong answer and target those topics
Switch to a brand-new reference book immediately and start again
questions.why: Analysing mistakes improves scores faster than repeating tests.

questions.q: Your coding project keeps crashing. What's most effective?
o: Debug step by step and search for similar issues
Delete everything and rewrite the whole project from scratch right away
Ask someone to fix it for you
questions.why: Systematic debugging builds skill and solves problems.

questions.q: You lose an election for student council. What helps?
o: Congratulate the winner and find other ways to contribute
Withdraw from all school activities since the students didn't choose you
questions.why: Contributing in other ways shows true leadership.

questions.q: You feel stuck on a long-term goal. What can help?
o: Change to a new goal every week until you find one that feels easy
questions.why: Small milestones create momentum.

questions.q: You fail the first round of a music grade exam. What's best?
o: Practise the weak areas and book another attempt
Decide music isn't really for you and choose a different hobby
questions.why: Targeted practice leads to success.

questions.q: You lose a close friendship. What helps you move on?
o: Reflect on what you learned and invest in other relationships
Keep checking their social media to understand what went wrong
questions.why: Reflection and new connections help healing.

questions.q: You keep missing your study targets. What's a practical step?
o: Set even bigger daily targets so you push yourself harder
Study only when you feel like it
questions.why: Realistic targets build consistency.

questions.q: You get a harsh review for your creative work online. What's healthy?
o: Take useful points and ignore personal attacks
Delete all your work so nobody can criticise it again
questions.why: Separating feedback from attacks protects your motivation.

questions.q: Your plan to study abroad falls through. What's a resilient response?
o: Explore other good options and keep improving your profile
Give up on higher studies for now and start working immediately
questions.why: There are many paths to the same goal.

questions.q: You're injured before a big tournament. What helps?
o: Focus on recovery and support your team
Quit the sport for good and skip all of the team's matches this season
